jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer
jobs.description:
Ready to design the equipment behind circular concrete?

At everox, we transforming waste concrete into high-quality drop-in substitutes for cement, aggregates and sand. Our mission is to reduce global CO₂ emissions by 2% by phasing out the use of virgin materials in concrete via the patented everox waste concrete upcycling process.

We are now moving from pilots to industrial production. At our Rotterdam test site we develop and validate our process on small-scale pilots and in our own labs. Our first commercial facility in 's-Gravendeel is the next big step. After that: a second flagship plant abroad and new modular product lines that bring our technology to customers in containerised form.

**About the role**
------------------

As Mechanical Engineer, you are the 3D modelling and design strength of our mechanical team. You turn design input into accurate 3D models and drawings, and you are just as comfortable with your hands on the equipment.

The position sits in a small, hands-on engineering team of mechanical, process and automation engineers, reporting to our CTO. Besides your own projects, you work on the projects of both our Senior Mechanical Engineers: one focuses on our ’s-Gravendeel plant and future facilities, the other on our new containerised product lines.

Day to day, the work brings you together with these seniors, our process engineers and R&D, so you will receive direct coaching and build a broad knowledge of our technology from day one. Half of the time goes to our new modular product line, the other half to our test site, the operating facility in ’s-Gravendeel and the next international plants. International travel is part of the role for engineering reviews, factory acceptance tests, construction and commissioning of new plants.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* Create 3D models, drawings and bills of materials based on design input from our Senior Mechanical Engineers, for our containerised products, pilots, prototypes and plant modifications.
* Turn concepts, sketches and redlines into complete drawing and fabrication packages, and keep our CAD models, drawing standards and part libraries consistent and up to date.
* Perform mechanical calculations, select components, request and compare quotations, and review supplier documentation.
* Complete the commissioning of our pilot-scale carbonation reactor and hand it over to R&D.
* Design and implement modifications on our small-scale pilots for carbonation, milling, crushing and sieving, and build and test prototypes together with R&D, for example for continuous carbonation.
* Prepare the mechanical design of modifications on our ’s-Gravendeel facility under management of change (MOC), and support the review of mechanical deliverables for the next flagship plant.
* Take part in FAT/SAT, installation and commissioning on site.
* Maintain mechanical documentation and revision control, contribute to risk assessments and design reviews, and help build a strong safety culture on site.

**What you bring**
------------------

We are looking for a mechanical engineer with a few years of experience who is as comfortable in a 3D model as next to a piece of equipment on site. Turning someone else’s input into an accurate model appeals to you, and when that input is incomplete, you ask the right questions. You want to learn from experienced engineers and grow in mechanical design, and you see pilots and prototypes as a chance to get your hands dirty.

* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.
* 3 to 4 years of experience in mechanical design and project execution, for example in machine building or industrial equipment.
* Strong skills in 3D parametric CAD (Autodesk Inventor preferred), including assemblies, drawings and bills of materials.
* The ability to turn input from others into accurate models and drawings.
* A hands-on, practical attitude: comfortable assembling, testing and troubleshooting equipment.
* Experience with, or a strong interest in, pilot, prototype or test installations.
* Fluent English; Dutch language skills are a plus.
* Willingness to travel internationally for engineering reviews, FAT and commissioning.

**Nice-to-haves:**

* Experience with bulk solids handling equipment, such as crushers, mills or screens.
* Experience with skid-mounted or containerised equipment.
* Experience with Autodesk Vault or another PDM system.
* Basic knowledge of CE marking and pressure equipment.
* A VCA certificate.

**What we offer**
-----------------

* Competitive compensation based on the market, your experience and qualifications (€55,000-€65,000 gross per year including holiday allowance).
* Employee ownership through our ESOP and a company pension plan at Zwitserleven.
* 27 days of annual holiday leave.
* A one-year contract for 40 hours per week, with the intention to extend to a permanent contract.
* Training and development, including vendor training where relevant.
* Coaching by two Senior Mechanical Engineers, working side by side on their projects.
* An impactful position in a fast-growing, mission-driven scale-up.

**Why join us?**
----------------

We are a dynamic, diverse and international team located at SubZero, a hub for Greentech start-ups in the Port of Rotterdam. Our flat hierarchy gives you ownership of your work and room to grow, and the chance to help shape the engineering standards of a company moving from its first plant to multiple plants and products.

**Interested?**
---------------

Ready to design the equipment that turns waste concrete into new building materials? We would like to hear from you.

Even if you don’t meet every requirement, please apply - your unique background could be exactly what we need.

Founded in 2017 in Utrecht, Vitestro is pioneering the future of blood collection with the **Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™)**. This groundbreaking medical device combines advanced multi-modal imaging (near-infrared, ultrasound, and Doppler ultrasound) with robotics and AI to perform the entire diagnostic blood draw procedure autonomously.

By addressing critical healthcare staffing shortages and improving patient experience, Vitestro is transforming one of the most common and essential medical procedures. With more than 130 team members and growing rapidly, we are scaling our impact. As we placed our first devices with customers, we are now expanding our team to ensure successful implementation and long-term reliability.

At Vitestro, we are committed to continuous innovation and improvement.

**Your role**

“As our Mechanical Engineer in the Consumable Handling team, you design the mechanical subsystems behind some of Aletta’s key functions: the structural frame and housing that carries every other system, the safe disposal of used needles and filled blood tubes, the presentation of bandages, and the delivery of contact liquid and vacuum. It is a broad, integration-heavy role spanning mechanical structure, fluidics and actuation. You translate sub-system requirements into robust designs, integrate them into the wider device, and keep improving them based on production and field data. You build manufacturability, reliability and serviceability into the design from the start, so they are not added afterwards. You work closely with fellow mechanical, electrical, software, production and service colleagues.”

**First months at Vitestro**

“In your first months, you start the concept design for the mobility of our device in the hospital, so Aletta becomes easier to move and position wherever it is needed. At the same time, you update and verify our existing sub-system designs using what we learned from the first production runs, service activities and customer feedback. You turn these real-world findings into concrete design improvements and make sure they are verified and documented. You also start concept work on new UIS concepts, which shapes the next generation of our consumable handling.”

**This is what success looks like**

“After 12 months, you are recognized within the engineering team for your strong experience in Design for X (DfX), and you have helped incorporate DfX principles into the mechanical engineering community at Vitestro. Your designs move smoothly into production, hold up reliably in the field, and are easy to service. Colleagues come to you for your depth of knowledge, and you help raise the bar for how we design across the team.

You enjoy finishing what you start. You like to see a design all the way through, and you take the details seriously. You thrive in a multidisciplinary environment and bring a pragmatic, hands-on mentality to every challenge.”

At Vitestro, ownership is not a slogan - it is an expectation. We trust people to take responsibility, make decisions, and drive work forward.

We believe breakthroughs happen when talented people combine dedication, accountability, and teamwork. That means:

* We take initiative rather than wait for direction.

### **What to Expect**

We build electric motorcycles. The engineering underneath them needs to be as deliberate, reliable, and honest as the ride itself — and this role is central to making that true. The Mechanical Design Engineer IV is an autonomous technical contributor and practitioner who drives component and system-level development without requiring design guidance or mentoring. Operating from Zero's Netherlands office, this engineer leads mechanical design work across powertrain enclosures, high-voltage (HV) battery pack mechanical systems, vehicle structures, and cross-functional system integration — collaborating directly with programme management, industrial design, supply chain, and OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) partners. At this level, the engineer is a practitioner others learn from: technically deep, methodical in decision-making, and highly effective at translating system requirements into production-ready hardware.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**Technical Leadership & Design Ownership**

* Leads design and development of complex motorcycle components and systems — including structural frames, battery enclosures, IP-rated sealing systems, and powertrain integration — through all programme phases (concept, F&D (Feasibility and Definition), D&R (Durability and Refinement), VAL (Validation), FPCS (First Production Conforming Sample))
* Owns the full technical definition of assigned line items: 3D CAD master models, GD&T drawings, DFM/DFA analysis, DFMEA facilitation, DVP&R (Design Verification Plan and Report) planning, and production release in SAP ECTR
* Drives design decisions independently using sound engineering judgement; communicates trade-offs and recommendations clearly to programme leads and management
* Leads design reviews at key programme gates; prepares and presents technically rigorous review packages, incorporating cross-functional feedback effectively
* Identifies and resolves critical path risks in design and integration; escalates unresolvable conflicts with full technical framing

**Battery Pack & High-Voltage Mechanical Integration**

* Leads mechanical design of HV battery pack structural and sealing systems, including enclosure design, thermal interface material (TIM) specification, module retention, and bus bar / interconnect packaging
* Defines mechanical interface requirements between the pack and vehicle structure, BMS (Battery Management System) electronics, cooling circuits, and regulatory compliance hardware
* Applies knowledge of UN 38.3 (transport testing), IEC 62619 (safety requirements for stationary and traction batteries), and relevant homologation standards (EU Type Approval, AIS-156 for India-market programmes where applicable) to design decisions
* Owns DFM/DFA review for battery pack assemblies; coordinates PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) readiness activities with supply chain and manufacturing engineering

**Vehicle Systems & Integration**

* Collaborates at vehicle architecture level with programme CPL (Chief Platform Lead), ID (Industrial Design), powertrain, and electrical teams to resolve packaging conflicts and meet system-level requirements
* Owns or contributes to major structural design (frame interfaces, swingarm, headlight structure, tail section) and dynamic structure design (impact load paths)
* Applies simulation tools — FEA (Altair HyperWorks or equivalent), CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics), thermal analysis — to validate design decisions before physical builds; interprets and acts on analysis results independently

**Supplier & Manufacturing Engagement**

* Leads technical engagement with part manufacturers, tooling suppliers, and contract development partners on assigned systems
* Reviews and approves supplier DFM feedback, prototype builds, and PPAP submission packages
* Responds to and leads root-cause analysis for manufacturing non-conformances and field failures within assigned scope

**Required Education / Experience**

* Bachelor of Science (B.S.) or higher in Mechanical Engineering
* 7+ years of relevant mechanical design engineering experience in a product development environment; motorcycle, automotive, or e-mobility industry strongly preferred
* Advanced SolidWorks proficiency: complex part modelling, advanced surfacing, large assembly management, master modelling methodology, full drawing and GD&T annotation
* Comprehensive understanding of manufacturing processes: injection moulding, casting (die and sand), forging, CNC machining, weldments, sheet metal fabrication, surface treatments, and composites

**Ben jij onze nieuwe collega?**
--------------------------------

Wil jij werken aan techniek die letterlijk de grenzen van de aarde overstijgt? Bij SRON werk je aan instrumentatie voor ruimteonderzoek: van testopstellingen en toepassingen voor grondtelescopen en stratosferische ballonnen tot instrumenten die uiteindelijk met een satelliet de ruimte in gaan. Ben jij een gedreven fijnmechanisch werktuigbouwer met een passie voor het ontwerpen en numeriek analyseren van complexe mechanieken? En krijg je energie van technische vraagstukken waarvoor niet meteen een standaardoplossing bestaat? Als constructeur bij SRON zet je jouw vakkennis, creativiteit en technische inzicht in om wetenschappers te ondersteunen bij baanbrekend onderzoek. Je werkt mee aan instrumenten die daadwerkelijk de ruimte in gaan en daarmee een bijdrage leveren aan onze kennis van het heelal. Klinkt dit als een uitdaging die bij jou past? Dan maken we graag kennis met je.

**Jouw functie**
----------------

Als constructeur ontwerp en analyseer je complexe onderdelen en samenstellingen voor instrumenten voor ruimteonderzoek. Daarbij krijg je te maken met een unieke combinatie van technische eisen. Denk aan extreme temperaturen, cryogene omstandigheden, vacuüm, straling en zeer hoge betrouwbaarheid. Bovendien moeten de instrumenten bestand zijn tegen de enorme krachten die tijdens een lancering optreden. Je werk beperkt zich niet tot het instrument zelf. Je draagt ook bij aan de ontwikkeling van laboratorium- en testopstellingen waarmee we onze instrumenten onder deze omstandigheden kunnen testen. Je werkt nauw samen met collega-constructeurs en ontwerpers uit andere disciplines, fysici en instrumentmakers. Samen onderzoek je mogelijke oplossingsrichtingen en vertaal je complexe wetenschappelijke en technische vraagstukken naar betrouwbare technische oplossingen. Kwaliteit loopt als een rode draad door je werk. Je hebt oog voor zowel de kwaliteit van het ontwerp als voor de processen waarmee het product wordt ontwikkeld, geproduceerd, samengesteld en getest. Je wordt onderdeel van het team Mechanica en bent regelmatig betrokken bij het produceren, samenbouwen en testen van jouw ontwerpen. Een groot deel hiervan vindt in-house plaats. Hierdoor zie je jouw ontwerp niet alleen op papier of in een CAD-model, maar daadwerkelijk tot leven komen. Binnen deze functie ligt het zwaartepunt op het numeriek analyseren van ontwerpen. Je werkt onder andere met Finite Element Methods (FEM) voor structurele analyses, zoals vibratie- en shock-spectra. Daarnaast voer je thermische en magneto-dynamische analyses uit. Je vertaalt de resultaten van deze analyses naar concrete verbeteringen en onderbouwde ontwerpkeuzes.

Tegelijkertijd blijf je constructeur in hart en nieren. Je ontwerpt en werkt oplossingen uit, legt deze technisch vast en maakt ze productierijp. Zo combineer je analytische diepgang met praktisch technisch inzicht.

**Jouw team**
-------------

Deze functie valt binnen de Sectie Mechanica van SRON’s Engineering Group (EG). Werken binnen een technische afdeling van een ruimtevaartinstituut is bijzonder. Hier draait het niet alleen om het realiseren van een goed ontwerp, maar vooral om zekerheid en betrouwbaarheid. Zodra een instrument de ruimte in gaat, is er immers geen mogelijkheid om het even open te maken, te repareren of een onderdeel te vervangen. Dat maakt het werk uitdagend én betekenisvol. Binnen ons engineeringteam werken we aan technische puzzels die soms bijna onmogelijk lijken. We ontwerpen, bouwen, testen, analyseren, leren en verbeteren. En als het nodig is, beginnen we opnieuw. Net zo lang totdat het werkt én we er volledig op kunnen vertrouwen. Juist die combinatie van uitdaging, vakmanschap en maatschappelijke en wetenschappelijke impact maakt het werk binnen onze Engineering Group zo interessant. Je werkt samen met gedreven specialisten die hun kennis willen inzetten voor iets dat groter is dan alleen het product: het vergroten van onze kennis over het heelal. Binnen de Engineering Group ontwikkelen, bouwen en testen we hightech mechanica en elektronica voor innovatieve wetenschappelijke instrumenten. We werken in kleine, dynamische teams waarin verschillende technische disciplines nauw samenwerken. Als constructeur word je onderdeel van het team binnen de Sectie Mechanica. Vanuit dit team werk je mee aan verschillende projecten die op dat moment binnen SRON worden uitgevoerd. Dat kunnen interne projecten zijn, maar ook projecten binnen internationale samenwerkingsverbanden met collega-instituten en hightech industriële partners. De projecten variëren sterk in omvang en looptijd: van enkele maanden tot projecten die zich over bijna twee decennia uitstrekken. Die variatie zorgt ervoor dat je steeds met nieuwe technische uitdagingen en samenwerkingspartners te maken krijgt. Bij het verdelen van projecten kijken we niet alleen naar wat er nodig is, maar ook naar jouw kennis, interesses en ambities. We vinden het belangrijk dat je werk aansluit bij jouw ontwikkeling en groeipad. Je krijgt veel ruimte om zelfstandig je werkzaamheden uit te voeren. Tegelijkertijd vraagt de functie om een proactieve houding en het vermogen om met verschillende stakeholders af te stemmen, soms verdeeld over meerdere projecten en disciplines. De dagelijkse werkzaamheden worden aangestuurd vanuit de projecten. Het sectiehoofd Mechanica bewaakt daarnaast jouw ontwikkeling, belangen en positie binnen de organisatie. Deze manier van werken past bij onze matrixorganisatie.

Voor deze functie kun je kiezen uit Groningen of Leiden als standplaats.

**Jouw project**

SRON is een wetenschappelijke instelling met een sterk academisch karakter. Er wordt de tijd en moeite genomen om technische en fysische aspecten diepgaand te beschouwen en evalueren om zo baanbrekende producten te realiseren die beter zijn dan alles wat ooit eerder is gedaan. As Senior Mechanical Engineer – Modular Products, you own and lead the mechanical engineering of our new containerised product lines. You also support our flagship plants: you engineer modifications on our operating facility in ’s-Gravendeel and review the mechanical engineering of the next flagship plant.

**About S E S C**

SESC is a specialist engineering services company providing MEP commissioning, quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC), and technical project support across complex projects and multiple industry sectors. We are developing our capabilities in existing-building surveys and as-found documentation, helping clients understand the actual condition and configuration of buildings where original as-built drawings are missing, incomplete, or no longer reflect site conditions.

We are seeking a practical, **technically minded CAD Engineer with a preference for an MEP background and some civil or structural knowledge. This role is suited to someone who enjoys working both on site and in the office, combining technical observation, measurement, drawing production, and multidisciplinary coordination.**

**This is not a purely office-based drafting position.** The successful candidate must be **willing to attend site inspections, take measurements, record existing conditions, and work directly with SESC engineers to produce accurate as-found drawings.**

The CAD Engineer will be responsible for surveying, documenting, and preparing as-found drawings of existing building conditions.

The candidate will work alongside the Structural Engineer and SESC's existing MEP commissioning engineers to investigate two auditoriums where reliable as-built documentation is limited.

The work will involve gathering information directly from the site, taking measurements, recording visible building elements and MEP installations, preparing sketches and photographic records, and converting verified information into organised initial 2D AutoCAD drawings.

The candidate will need to understand that **as-found drawings document observed and measured existing conditions; they are not automatically equivalent to approved design drawings or certified as-built drawings.**

* Assist the Structural Engineer in documenting relevant structural observations, without independently making structural engineering determinations.
* Prepare field sketches, measurement sheets, marked-up drawings, and photographic records.
